_comment: Scoped URLs restored AND VERIFIED 2026-09-03 (see docs/specs/built/SPEC_prod_mcp_oauth_restore.md).
Each entry carries its project_ref, and supabase-prod-readonly carries read_only=true.
VERIFIED, not assumed — prod is write-blocked at the server, not by per-call discipline:
read  'select count(*) from catalog_items'          -> 364 (dev returns 117: different DBs)
write 'update catalog_items set id = id where false' -> ERROR: 25006: cannot execute UPDATE
in a read-only transaction
25006 is a Postgres SQLSTATE (read_only_sql_transaction) — the statement reached the database
and was refused inside a transaction already opened READ ONLY. Enforcement lives in the OAuth
grant, downstream of this file. read_only=true also SHRINKS THE TOOL SURFACE: the prod server
does not advertise apply_migration, deploy_edge_function, or any branch tool, so the
'deploy executable code to prod' hole flagged 2026-09-02 is closed as well.
IF OAUTH FAILS with 'resource: Resource must be a valid MCP endpoint':
That is Claude Code issue #34880 — CLOSED AS NOT PLANNED, so do not wait for a patch. It is
scoped to the Claude Code panel inside the VS Code extension, which double-encodes the '?'
when building the OAuth 'resource' parameter. The terminal CLI does not have this bug.
Do NOT fix it by stripping the query string: that silently removes read_only=true and
re-opens prod to writes. Instead, quit VS Code, run 'claude' in a plain terminal window, and
complete /mcp OAuth there. Tokens then carry over to the VS Code panel (confirmed 2026-09-03
— the verification queries above were run from the panel on terminal-issued tokens), so only
the HANDSHAKE must happen outside VS Code, not everyday use.
